minutes.headline: Conservation Commission continued most hearings for missing DEP numbers and kept its current officers.
minutes.summary: The commission heard several notices of intent and requests for determination. It issued negative determinations for a slope repair at Sunset Lane and for tree removal at Fire Road 19, and continued most other hearings to September 4 for lack of DEP file numbers. It read through proposed wetlands regulation revisions, agreed on a definition of structure, and reappointed its officers.

public_comment.topic: An abutter objected to the proposed catch basin, walls and riprap encroaching on his property at the Sunset Lane retaining wall hearing, and favored a continuance.

Reappoint the current officers (chair, vice chair, clerk, treasurer) by roll call

budget_items.what_was_said: Proposed regulation changes to the fee schedule: subdivision fee gets a per-foot charge and commercial fees are replaced by a per-square-foot charge.

budget_items.what_was_said: Fines for violations revised to a maximum per day, and daily offence fines set within a range.

decisions.decision: Applicant at 43 Fire Road 19 must plant two 8 to 10 foot trees and two shrubs.
A straw poll of commissioners favored changing the wall footprint at Sunset Lane to save the large trees.
Applicant at 131/133 Lunenburg Shirley Road is asked for stormwater basin calculations, riverfront alteration numbers and a report from the wetland consultant on the pipe elevation.
The owner at 127 Pleasant Street is to work with the agent on a plan and be heard on September 4; a cease and desist was issued.
Commission agreed to add a definition of structure and the words permanent and temporary structures to the regulations.
The September 4 meeting will be at the Ritter building, with regulation revision added as a discussion item.

what_happened.line: The commission continued most hearings to September 4, several for missing DEP file numbers and one because abutters were not notified.
It voted negative determinations for the slope repair at 380 Sunset Lane and for tree removal at 43 Fire Road 19, which requires replacement planting.
A cease and desist was issued at 127 Pleasant Street; the owner is to work with the agent on a plan and be heard September 4.
The commission read through proposed wetlands regulation revisions, including changes to filing fees and violation fines, and agreed to add a definition of structure.
The current officers were reappointed by roll call.

why_it_matters: Wetlands filing fees and violation fines are proposed to change, which would affect what applicants and property owners near wetlands pay, and the revised definition of structure sets what the rules cover.
Projects on Sunset Lane, Northfield Road and Lunenburg Shirley Road remain undecided, so neighbors and abutters will see them again at the next hearing.
watch_next: September 4 meeting at the Ritter building, where the continued hearings return and the regulation revision is a discussion item.
